name: ChronDB
headline: A database that starts with the question: what was true then?
standfirst: ChronDB puts Git-style history at the centre of a key/value store. Compatibility is the harder half of the idea.
evidence: Public repository and README only. No ChronDB process or client workload was run by Toolglass.

body.heading: What is it?
paragraphs: ChronDB is a key/value database organised around chronological history and branching. The pitch is simple to state and difficult to make useful: ask not only what a value is, but what it used to be.

body.heading: Why did Radar notice it?
paragraphs: Most teams bolt an audit trail onto a database after the fact. ChronDB treats history as the starting point. That makes it an unusually clear experiment in whether familiar database access can coexist with a versioned model underneath.

body.heading: What's the catch?
paragraphs: A protocol name is not feature parity. Transactions, restart recovery, query coverage and operational cost still need to be measured against the application you actually have.

verdict: A genuinely odd database idea that deserves a careful client-compatibility test before anyone calls it a replacement.
nextStep: Define a tiny workload, then test historical reads, branching and restart recovery.
